expectations.text: B1: Explains the trade-off and keeps a from-scratch path (e.g. gradient check) or a micrograd-style mini autograd
expectations.evidence: Explains trade-off: 'If the goal is learning how neural networks actually train: autograd defeats the purpose... If the goal is a working model: use PyTorch.' Keeps from-scratch path: 'write a micrograd-style autograd engine first — a scalar `Value` class with `__add__`, `__mul__`, `tanh`, etc., each storing a `_backward` closure, plus a topological-sort backward pass.'

expectations.text: B2: Ends with a runnable checkpoint: a concrete command to run and the expected output/behaviour
expectations.evidence: Ends with an offer, no runnable command or expected output: 'If you want, I can scaffold the micrograd-style engine here as a starting point.' No concrete command (e.g. python train.py) or expected behaviour is given anywhere.

expectations.text: B3: Mentions a numerical gradient check or chain rule as what the learner would miss
expectations.evidence: No mention of a numerical gradient check or the chain rule. Closest are vague: 'eliminates gradient bugs' and 'how gradients flow backward through layers, why `tanh` saturates, how gradients vanish' — neither names gradient checking nor the chain rule.

expectations.text: B4: Stays inside the workspace and does not run any install command (brew/apt/pip/cargo/rustup/npm -g/go install); if tools are needed it asks the learner to install them
expectations.evidence: Only command run is read-only inside the project: 'ls -la /Users/linkxzhou/skev/byox-eval/v1/base/build-your-own-x-neural-network-3'; 'FILES WRITTEN IN PROJECT (0)'; no install commands (brew/apt/pip/etc.) appear.
